title: DNA extraction from wheat leaf tissue
author: Benjamin Schwessinger
materials: The demonstrator will rupture your tissue using a TissueLyzer II https://www.qiagen.com/us/products/human-id-and-forensics/automation/tissuelyser-ii at 25 Hz for 1 min. Now the leaf rupture part of the protocol is complete.
Discard the DNeasy Mini spin column.

steps.title: Label tubes and beads
steps.instruction: Label each 2 ml Eppendorf tube that will contain 2–3 steel beads with the treatment‑group (TG) name and your research‑group name on both the top and the side of the tube.

steps.title: Select and cut leaf samples
steps.instruction: Inspect the plants in each pot, choose two leaves per TG that show representative symptoms (TG #1‑4) or no symptoms for the negative control (TG #5). Cut 1.5–2 cm long middle leaf pieces from each of the two independent leaves and place both pieces into the correctly labelled tube.

steps.title: Freeze leaf samples
steps.instruction: After all five TGs are prepared, freeze the tubes immediately in liquid nitrogen with the demonstrator; the demonstrator will collect all tubes for one bench row before tissue rupture.

steps.title: Keep samples on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tubes containing leaf material on ice or keep them frozen on liquid nitrogen as handled by the demonstrator.

steps.title: Prepare labeled spin‑column sets
steps.instruction: Label all provided tubes and spin columns with the TG name and research‑group name. For each TG prepare: a QIAshredder spin column (pink) placed in a 2 ml collection tube, one additional 2 ml collection tube, two 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes, and a DNeasy Mini spin column (blue) placed in a 2 ml collection tube. You will have five identical sets ready for parallel DNA extraction.

steps.title: Add Buffer AP1 and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 400 µl Buffer AP1 to each 2 ml tube containing the ruptured leaf tissue, then vortex until the tissue is completely resuspended in the buffer.

steps.title: Add RNase A and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 4 µl RNase A to each tube and vortex again; RNase A works best at 65 °C.

steps.title: Incubate at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for 10 min at 65 °C in a water bath or heating block, inverting each tube 2–3 times during the incubation.

steps.title: Hand‑centrifuge to collect lysate
steps.instruction: Hand‑centrifuge each tube as demonstrated (hold the top of the tube and give a rapid ‘throw’ motion) to collect the lysate at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Add Buffer P3 and mix
steps.instruction: Add 130 µl Buffer P3 to each tube and mix by inverting 10–20 times immediately after addition to clear the lysate.

steps.title: Cool and ice incubations
steps.instruction: Hand‑centrifuge again, then cool the tubes on ice for 2 min followed by an additional 5 min incubation on ice (longer incubation does not affect outcome).

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate 5 min
steps.instruction: Balance the centrifuge, ensure all tubes are clearly labelled, and centrifuge the lysates for 5 min at maximum speed to pellet larger undissolved particles.

steps.title: Load lysate onto QIAshredder
steps.instruction: Pipette 480 µl of the cleared lysate into the QIAshredder spin column (placed in a 2 ml collection tube) for each TG, taking care not to disturb any pellet.

steps.title: Centrifuge QIAshredder
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the QIAshredder spin columns for 2 min at maximum speed and keep the flow‑through in the lower collection tube.

steps.title: Transfer flow‑through
steps.instruction: Transfer 400 µl of the flow‑through into a new clearly labelled 1.5 ml tube for each TG, avoiding disturbance of any pellet.

steps.title: Add Buffer AW1 and mix
steps.instruction: Add 600 µl Buffer AW1 to each tube and mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Bind DNA to DNeasy column
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µl of the mixture into the DNeasy Mini spin column (placed in a 2 ml collection tube) for each TG; all tubes and columns must be clearly labelled.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard flow‑through
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the DNeasy Mini spin columns for 1 min at maximum speed, then discard the flow‑through into a waste container.

steps.title: Add remaining lysate and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Add the remaining ~500 µl sample onto the same DNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuge for 1 min at maximum speed; discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: First wash with Buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Place the spin column into a new clearly labelled 2 ml collection tube, add 500 µl Buffer AW2 on top of the column (do not touch the membrane with the tip), centrifuge 1 min at maximum speed, discard flow‑through, and tap the collection tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Second wash with Buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Place the spin column back into a new 2 ml collection tube, add another 500 µl Buffer AW2, centrifuge for 2 min at maximum speed, discard flow‑through, and tap dry on a paper towel.

steps.title: Third wash with Buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Place the spin column again into a new 2 ml collection tube, add a third 500 µl Buffer AW2, centrifuge for 1 min at maximum speed, discard flow‑through, and tap the tube on a paper towel.

steps.title: Transfer column to elution tube
steps.instruction: Remove the DNeasy Mini spin column carefully so it does not contact the flow‑through, and transfer it to a new clearly labelled 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: First elution with Buffer AE
steps.instruction: Add 75 µl Buffer AE directly onto the centre of the membrane, incubate 5 min at room temperature (15–25 °C), then centrifuge for 1 min at maximum speed to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Second elution with Buffer AE
steps.instruction: Add another 75 µl Buffer AE onto the centre of the membrane, incubate 5 min at room temperature (15–25 °C), and centrifuge for 1 min at maximum speed to collect the second eluate.

steps.title: Store DNA eluate tubes
steps.instruction: Close each collection tube and keep it; you should now have five clearly labelled tubes each containing ~150 µl DNA in elution buffer (one TG per tube).

steps.title: Hand over tubes for storage
steps.instruction: Hand over the five clearly labelled DNA eluate tubes to the demonstrator for storage until the following week.
